# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
(Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals)
**Fax:** 859-425-3379
**Mail:** [Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Jordan Novak
**Member ID:** W423994730
**Plan:** Aetna (Commercial/ACA), North Dakota

**RE: Appeal of the denial dated 2026-08-18 — Reference number POC-570CD9F39B-59936**
**Service denied:** Lower back (lumbar) fusion, CPT 22612
**Governing policy:** *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)* — https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Aetna's denial of prior authorization for the lumbar fusion my surgeon has requested for me. The notice dated 2026-08-18 states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. The notice does not identify which document or which criterion was missing. I am asking you to reconsider that decision, and I am writing to show that the records already submitted match the plan's own published criteria in *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)*. If something specific is still needed, I would like to be told what it is so I can send it.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Instability on dynamic imaging.** The policy states:

> "Radiographic documentation dynamic instability of at least 4 mm of translation or 10 degrees of angular motion on dynamic imaging that has failed 6 weeks of conservative management"

My imaging of 2026-07-06 included flexion-extension radiographs of the lumbar spine showing **5 mm of translation** at L4-L5 — above the 4 mm the plan itself names. My conservative care spans well beyond six weeks: supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, **8 weeks and 20 visits, from 2026-05-24 to 2026-07-19**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note; **NSAIDs for 6 months** with inadequate relief; and a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-29** that gave only two weeks of partial relief. My symptoms have continued for 14 months and are progressive.

**2. Spondylolisthesis with segmental instability.** The policy states:

> "Spondylolisthesis with segmental instability confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI), with associated symptomatic unremitting low back pain, radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication, when either of the following criteria are met"

That sentence ends by introducing a list of conditions that I have not been given in full, so I cannot address every item; I ask that the plan identify the specific sub-criteria it applied. What my records do show is each element stated above: MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-07-06 confirming **grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5**, segmental instability on flexion-extension films, **14 months of progressive low back and leg pain unrelieved by rest**, and **neurogenic claudication** on examination — I cannot stand or walk more than 10 minutes before leg pain and heaviness force me to stop, and sitting relieves it.

**3. Spinal stenosis with anterolisthesis.** The policy states:

> "Spinal stenosis, where criteria for lumbar decompression in Section I.C. above are met, and any of the following is met: Decompression is performed in an area of segmental instability as manifested by gross movement on flexion-extension radiographs; or Decompression coincides with any degree of anterolisthesis (grades I, II, III, IV or V))"

My MRI shows **severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina**, and my listhesis is **grade I** — a degree the policy expressly includes. I was not provided the text of Section I.C., so I am unable to walk through it point by point here; if the denial rests on that section, please tell me which of its requirements you found unmet.

**4. Conservative measures.** The policy states:

> "Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression."

All of my conservative care falls within the past year: supervised physical therapy, 20 visits over 8 weeks ending 2026-07-19, documented in a discharge note; NSAIDs for 6 months without adequate relief; and an injection on 2026-05-29. If any additional record is needed on this point — for example [documentation of patient education, if the plan requires a separate record of it] — I will provide it on request.

**5. Surgeon's examination.** The policy states:

> "Medical records must document that a physical examination, including a neurologic examination, has been performed by or reviewed by the operating surgeon."

The prior authorization packet contains examination findings including neurogenic claudication and **diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes**, with no bowel or bladder dysfunction. My operating surgeon is **Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery**, who has documented that this procedure is needed. If confirmation of authorship is what was missing, please request [date and author of the operating surgeon's examination note] and it will be sent.

**6. Other items in the policy.** The records also note that I have **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker**. The policy contains further criteria addressing conditions that are not the basis of my surgery — including scoliosis, pseudarthrosis after prior fusion, flatback syndrome, fracture, pars defects in members under 18, spinal infection, and spinal tumor — and a criterion regarding hemoglobin A1C for members who are diabetic. If any of those provisions were applied in reviewing my request, please identify which, and I will supply [any additional records the plan specifies, such as laboratory values, if applicable].

## What I am asking for

Because the denial was issued for incomplete documentation without naming what was missing, I ask Aetna to:

1. Reconsider and overturn the denial of CPT 22612 and approve the requested lumbar fusion; or
2. If the decision is not changed, tell me in writing the specific criterion from *Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion (CPB 0743)* that was not met and the specific document that was found to be missing, so that I can supply it; and
3. Provide a copy of the full criteria relied upon, including the list introduced by the spondylolisthesis criterion and Section I.C. referenced in the stenosis criterion.

I am submitting this appeal within the period stated in my denial notice, which says my appeal must be received within 180 days of 2026-08-18, by **2027-02-14**. I am sending it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form from my account at aetna.com, by fax to 859-425-3379 or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, and I can be reached by phone through 1-800-872-3862 or the number on my card.

I would appreciate your careful review. I am able to send any additional records quickly if you will tell me what is needed.

Sincerely,

**Jordan Novak**

Reference number: POC-570CD9F39B-59936

Lumbar pseudarthrosis (defined as absence of bridging bone that connects the vertebrae, or movement of vertebrae at site of prior attempted arthrodesis on dynamic radiographs) after 12 months have elapsed since the time of fusion

For lumbar pseudoarthrosis not associated with hardware failure or indications for urgent intervention, the member should be nicotine-free (including smoking, use of tobacco products, and nicotine replacement therapy) for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery.

Iatrogenic or degenerative flatback syndrome (defined as members with back pain, stooped posture and limitation of forward gaze), and with significant sagittal imbalance that has failed 3 months of conservative management

Spinal fracture causing instability or neural element compromise/compression, spinal dislocation (associated with mechanical instability), locked facets, or fracture with displaced fracture fragment confirmed by advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) causing neural element compromise, which may be combined with a laminectomy.

Pars defects (fractures) without significant instability (for spondylolisthesis/instability follow criteria (9) below) and with disc degeneration at the surgical level in members under 18 years of age who have failed at least 6 months of conservative management that includes bracing and at least 6 weeks of formal in-person physical therapy within the past year
Spinal infection confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI) and/or other studies (e.g., biopsy), which may be combined with a laminectomy
Spinal tumor confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI), which may be combined with a laminectomy

Spondylolisthesis with segmental instability confirmed by imaging studies (e.g., CT or MRI), with associated symptomatic unremitting low back pain, radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication, when either of the following criteria are met
Radiographic documentation of significant spondylolisthesis, grades II, III, IV, or V (see Appendix ) that has failed six weeks of conservative management
Radiographic documentation dynamic instability of at least 4 mm of translation or 10 degrees of angular motion on dynamic imaging that has failed 6 weeks of conservative management

Spinal stenosis, where criteria for lumbar decompression in Section I.C. above are met, and any of the following is met: Decompression is performed in an area of segmental instability as manifested by gross movement on flexion-extension radiographs; or Decompression coincides with any degree of anterolisthesis (grades I, II, III, IV or V))

Conservative measures must be recent (within the past year) and include the following non-surgical measures and medications unless one or more of the requirements for waiver below are met: patient education; active physical therapy (in-person as opposed to home or virtual physical therapy); medications (NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or tricyclic antidepressants), and (where appropriate) identification and management of associated anxiety and depression.

If member is diabetic, their hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) should be less than 8 percent within 3 months prior to surgery, unless there is an urgent indication for surgery (e.g., myelopathy, cauda equina syndrome), severe weakness (graded 4 minus or less on Medical Research Council [MRC] scale) or progressive weakness, or an associated infection/tumor and/or acute fracture.
Medical records must document that a physical examination, including a neurologic examination, has been performed by or reviewed by the operating surgeon.

an offset of greater than 5 cm between the sagittal vertebral axis (a plumb line downward from the center of the C7 vertebral body) and the posterior superior aspect of the S1 vertebral body; or a pelvic tilt greater than 20 degrees; or a lumbar lordosis to pelvic incidence mismatch of greater than or equal to 10 degrees
